page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-focused instance configuration powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 40 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 80.0 GB, establishing a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned without local storage disks, requiring attached persistent storage, and contains no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show high computational throughput across parallel workloads. In synthetic CPU metrics, the instance achieves top 25% results with a multi-core score of 107952.86 in stress-ng and an overall PassMark CPU score of 69646.99. Hardware-assisted cryptography performs in the top 10% tier on the PassMark encryption test at 85363.22. Memory performance is robust, delivering uncached read bandwidth of 187.06 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 109.12 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates high concurrency handling, logging 77.49 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong 43413.0 score in Clang software compilation.

Cost efficiency is centered on high core density, delivering strong compute and parallel processing performance per resource unit without the added expense of excess RAM or local disk enclosures. The trade-off is the constrained 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU, which limits utility for memory-heavy databases or large in-memory caches. Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is targeted for parallelized CPU tasks, Clang software builds, distributed batch processing, physics modeling, and compute-intensive microservices.

Lacking local storage and GPU hardware, the instance relies on network-attached storage while emphasizing CPU throughput. In performance evaluations, it achieves strong multi-core results, including 107952.86 in stress-ng multi-core testing, top-tier cryptographic speeds of 85363.22 in PassMark encryption, and 77.49 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio maximizes core density for CPU-bound tasks, offering efficient compute throughput while requiring external disk attachments. Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is suited for software compilation pipelines, batch processing, encryption services, and parallelized data processing workloads.
